index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure illustrates an autonomous vehicle (AV) network operating within a defined road environment, depicted as a rectangular area bounded by dashed lines. The global layout is vertically divided into two lanes separated by a double white line, representing a two-way road. Above the road, a blue 3D building icon labeled 'Building' is positioned at the top-left corner, symbolizing a central infrastructure or control node. Within the road area, three black car icons represent autonomous vehicles: one labeled 'Agent' on the lower left lane, another labeled 'AV₁' on the lower right lane, and a third labeled 'AV₂' in the upper lane. These vehicles are arranged to show spatial relationships and communication patterns.

Visual modules include the building, the three AVs, and the road. The building is a blue cube with white windows, indicating a fixed infrastructure component. The AVs are stylized black cars with visible wheels and windows; each is labeled with its respective identifier ('Agent', 'AV₁', 'AV₂') in black text near or above the vehicle. The road is represented as a gray rectangular region with a horizontal double white line dividing it into two lanes. A legend at the bottom of the figure defines two types of links: a dashed arrow labeled 'Communication link' and a solid double-headed arrow labeled 'Sensing link'.

Connections and arrows depict interactions between entities. Communication links are shown as dashed lines with arrowheads, indicating bidirectional data exchange. The Agent communicates with both AV₁ and AV₂ via dashed lines, and AV₁ also communicates with AV₂. Additionally, both AV₁ and AV₂ have dashed communication links extending upward to the Building, suggesting connectivity to a central network. Sensing links are represented by solid double-headed arrows, indicating mutual perception or detection. A solid double-headed arrow connects the Agent and AV₁, signifying direct sensing between them. The figure also includes a dashed line from the lower-right corner of the road boundary pointing downward to the label 'The road', anchoring the physical environment. The overall structure emphasizes a networked system where AVs exchange information both among themselves and with a central infrastructure, while also sensing their immediate surroundings.
